status_summary: On 2025-02-25 the White House announced that it, not the White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA), would decide which outlets make up the travelling press pool, and in its 2025-03-11 opposition in Associated Press v. Budowich (D.D.C. No. 25-0532, ECF 33) the government states that the WHCA set pool membership through that date and that the White House now selects the pool from television, wire and subject-matter groups. On 2025-04-15 the White House ended the wire services' permanent pool slot (Reuters via Malay Mail), and on 2025-08-11 the President declined a suggestion for a larger briefing room, with no decision on permanent press workspace found. The Associated Press won a preliminary injunction on 2025-04-08 that a divided D.C. Circuit panel stayed except for the East Room on 2025-06-06; the appeal (No. 25-5109) was argued on 2025-11-24 with no merits decision found. On 2026-10-13 Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C. No. 26-3287, ECF 50) granted a preliminary injunction requiring restoration of the revoked hard passes of CNN, MS NOW and Politico employees and denied a stay pending appeal, a ruling on access that does not address the press pool or the WHCA; the government noticed an appeal on 2026-10-14 (TheWrap, Virginia Mercury).

timeline.event: Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announces that the White House will decide which outlets make up the press pool, a role the WHCA had performed through a rotation of its members; the WHCA's president objects. The government's 2025-02-28 court notice describes the announced change as designed to open access to outlets that had not historically been pool members.

In its opposition to the Associated Press's preliminary injunction motion, the government states that the WHCA determined pool membership through 2025-02-25, that the pool is now selected by the White House itself (television, wire and subject-matter groups), and that the Oval Office, Air Force One (about thirteen press seats) and the East Room are space-limited; it reports that 310 journalists requested access to a 2025-02-24 East Room event and 136 were admitted.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (government filing)

timeline.event: Judge Trevor McFadden (D.D.C.) grants the Associated Press a preliminary injunction in Associated Press v. Budowich (No. 1:25-cv-00532), finding it likely to succeed on viewpoint-discrimination and retaliation claims over its exclusion from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other limited spaces. The opinion says the government may set reasonable, viewpoint-neutral limits on access and has no duty to admit all journalists. The court then stays the order on its own motion, and the government appeals the next day.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia

timeline.event: The White House says wire services (Reuters, Bloomberg, AP) lose their permanent pool slot and join a rotation with print outlets; the press secretary is to decide pool membership day to day. AP's report of 2025-04-17 quotes the policy as keeping that discretion with the press secretary.
A divided D.C. Circuit panel (2-1) grants the government's stay motion in part, so the injunction remains in force only for the East Room while the appeal proceeds.

The D.C. Circuit orders the government to respond to the Associated Press's emergency petition for rehearing en banc of the court's 2025-06-06 order, which partially granted the government's motion for a stay pending appeal.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

timeline.event: The full D.C. Circuit declines to rehear the stay order, leaving the AP exclusion from restricted spaces in place while the appeal continues; the court noted the stay order did not resolve the merits.
At a press event the President declines a reporter's suggestion to build a larger briefing room; the report describes no decision on a new press workspace.
The D.C. Circuit hears oral argument in the AP appeal (No. 25-5109); the litigation clearinghouse page, last updated 2026-07-22, lists no merits decision.
The President announces on social media that CNN, MS NOW and Politico are barred from the White House; their hard passes are revoked and taken at the West Wing gate on 2026-09-19.

Late on 2026-09-23 Judge Timothy Kelly (D.D.C., Cable News Network, Inc. v. Trump) orders the hard passes of CNN, MS NOW and Politico restored for 14 days, on a finding that the outlets are likely to show a due-process violation, and sets a preliminary-injunction briefing schedule; after the outlets report being turned away on 2026-09-24 and seek an emergency hearing, a White House official states in a court filing that the badges were restored, and the outlets regain access by about midday that day.
timeline.source: ABC News 4 (Sinclair); Idaho Capital Sun (States Newsroom)

timeline.event: Judge Timothy Kelly (D.D.C., Cable News Network, Inc. v. Trump) extends the temporary restraining order restoring the hard passes of CNN, MS NOW and Politico through 2026-10-13 and says he expects to rule on their preliminary injunction motion by then; the Justice Department asks that any injunction be limited to the passes and stayed pending appeal.

Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C., Cable News Network, Inc. v. Trump, No. 26-3287, ECF 50) grants a preliminary injunction extending the relief of the temporary restraining order, so that defendants other than the President must restore the revoked White House hard passes of CNN, MS NOW and Politico employees while the case proceeds. The opinion finds the outlets likely to succeed on Fifth Amendment notice and First Amendment retaliation and viewpoint-discrimination claims, denies the government's stay request and sets a nominal bond; it does not address press pool composition or the WHCA.

Justice Department attorneys file a notice of appeal to the D.C. Circuit from Judge Kelly's 2026-10-13 preliminary injunction in Cable News Network, Inc. v. Trump; reports say the notice contained no legal arguments, that the appeal does not suspend the injunction, that the government's brief is due 2026-11-13, and mention no stay motion. The Virginia Mercury text places the filing on Tuesday in its body and Wednesday in its lede; TheWrap gives Wednesday 2026-10-14. The court docket itself was not read.
